A1.justification: Both complete, readable 28-page PDFs describe the same RALU work and include Appendices A–E. Pages 2–28 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; differences are confined to page 1.

before.justification: v1 reports original RALU experiments on FLUX.1-dev and SD3, including quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–4 and qualitative experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those original quantitative results, ablations, and appendix qualitative experiments unchanged.

M1.justification: The three-stage RALU procedure, edge-based latent selection, NT-DM rescheduling, and caching integration are unchanged in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B.5.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same text-to-image coverage: GenEval, the complex and texture subsets of T2I-CompBench, and 96 CC12M prompts for uncurated examples. No datasets or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains reduced-step FLUX, ToCa, and Bottleneck Sampling; Table 2 retains reduced-step SD3, RAS, and Bottleneck Sampling. Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the qualitative comparisons.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, inference schedules, acceleration settings, baseline configurations, and sample counts are unchanged, including 2,212 GenEval images and 2,400 T2I-CompBench images in Appendix B.4.

E4.justification: The NT-DM parameter ablation in Table 4, upsampling-ratio analysis in Figure 6, upsampling-timing analysis in Figure S1, and additional qualitative examples are identical.

E5.justification: Appendix B.4 retains the same fixed-seed GenEval description and four-seed T2I-CompBench sampling. Neither version adds uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, RALU retains 7.02× speedup with FID 28.68 on FLUX in Table 1 and 3.02× with FID 23.29 on SD3 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The distribution-matching equations, covariance assumptions, optimization formulation, and Appendix A derivation of the noise-rescheduling coefficients are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free spatial acceleration, artifact suppression, approximately 7×/3× speedups on FLUX/SD3, and compatibility with caching.

C2.justification: Artifact explanations and speed–quality interpretations are unchanged. Appendix D retains the limitations concerning NT-DM's restriction to flow-matching models and untested generalization to other frameworks, architectures, and modalities.

D1.justification: v2 adds the RALU repository address, github.com/ignoww/RALU, beneath the author information; v1 lacks this access pointer. Implementation details and hardware disclosures are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish repository availability or contents.

R1.justification: The same 54 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning against Bottleneck Sampling and temporal caching methods. The new repository link does not revise research positioning.

P1.justification: Front-matter text gains the repository address, and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. Scientific prose, terminology, section organization, and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: The repository line and adjusted vertical spacing slightly alter page 1. All figures, tables, captions, and page layouts on pages 2–28 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The added front-page repository pointer modestly improves reproducibility documentation by identifying where readers can seek the implementation. Scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged. This limited benefit does not establish that the linked code is available, complete, or correct.
